Part 01

System Overview

Documents flow in through ingestion and queries flow in through retrieval; Milvus sits in the middle as the shared dual-vector store.

Designed and implemented Retrieval-Augmented Generation(RAG) service on FastAPI. It ingests documents, extracts a six-category knowledge tree with an LLM, stores dual-vector (content + summary) embeddings in Milvus, and answers queries by either synthesising a grounded answer or assembling an execution plan.

Technology stack

LayerTechnologyWhy
API frameworkFastAPIAsync-native, auto-generated OpenAPI docs, typed validation
Vector storeMilvus (Lite or Standalone)HNSW with COSINE metric; dual-field search (content + summary); tree-structured schema
Embedding modelmulti-qa-MiniLM-L6-cos-v1Asymmetric Q→passage model (384-dim); outperforms symmetric all-MiniLM on retrieval
LLM provideribm/granite-4-h-smallCalled over plain HTTP; enables rate-limit control and raw debug dumps

API surface

Everything is mounted under /api/v1. Interactive docs live at /docs (Swagger) and /redoc.

Part 02 · Write path

Ingestion Pipeline

Converts raw documents into structured, searchable dual-vector chunks stored in Milvus.

POST /api/v1/ingest/file.

2.1Loading & cleaning

Each source format is handled by a dedicated loader that outputs clean plain text; a universal cleaner then normalises all Unicode to ASCII.

SourceHow it is handled
PDFExtracts text and tables; font-size rank emits Markdown headings
TXT / MDReads plain UTF-8 text
HTMLStrips HTML tags
CSVSerialises rows to labelled text
JSONRecursively flattens key-value pairs

The universal text cleaner runs in four ordered passes:

  1. NFKC normalisation — collapses ligatures (ﬁ→fi) and full-width characters
  2. Transliteration — smart quotes → ", em-dash → -, NBSP → space, bullets → -, arrows → ->, ellipsis → ...
  3. NFKD accent stripping — é→e, ü→u
  4. Drop non-ASCII — any remaining byte outside printable ASCII is replaced with a space

2.2Windowing & chunking

Splits cleaned text into fixed-size overlapping windows before sending to the LLM, then applies fine-grained recursive splitting after extraction.

  • Window size — 8,000 tokens for now.
  • Overlap — 10% between consecutive windows so no context is lost at boundaries.
  • Recursive chunking — post-extraction rechunking with this separator ladder (coarse → fine):
"\n\n" → ". " → "? " → "! " → "; " → "\n" → " " → ""

2.3LLM extraction

Sends each window to the LLM and extracts six typed knowledge categories. Each category has both a scope (what it captures) and a strict summary contract (what its summary must contain), which keeps downstream summaries uniform and retrievable.

CategoryWhat it capturesSummary must capture
knowledgeProduct overview, architecture explanations, background conceptswhat the concept is · why it matters · how it fits the architecture
keywordsProduct terms, acronyms, component names, technical standardsthe term · its full name/expansion · a one-line definition
personasUsers who operate the productrole title · what they use the product for · key responsibilities
featuresNamed product capabilities or functionsname · definition · limitations/constraints · benefits · prerequisites
workflowsStep-by-step procedures, configuration tasks, operational processesgoal/outcome · prerequisites · the key ordered steps
entitiesNamed system objects — agents, policies, collectors, nodes, services, connectors, componentsentity name · what it does · how it relates to other components

Extraction modes trade speed against per-type fidelity:

ModeDescription
all_types (default)One LLM call per window extracts all 6 categories — fastest
parallelRouter inventories facts; 6 typed passes run concurrently — same speed, higher fidelity
sequentialRouter + 6 typed passes run as serial batches — slowest, highest accuracy

Rate-limit protection — requests are batched with a delay between groups; empty windows are auto-retried at reduced concurrency before giving up.

2.4Summarisation

Generates abstractive summaries for every chunk in three phases: leaf summaries, bottom-up hierarchical rollup, and a document-level overview.

Phase 1 — Leaf summaries. Each leaf chunk gets a 1–3 sentence abstractive summary written by a category-specific prompt:

CategorySummary structure
knowledgeDefinition → mechanism → purpose
keywordsACRONYM (Full Name): definition + function + purpose
personasRole → features used → why the product is needed
workflowsName + type → key steps → outcome
featuresCapability → constraints → benefit
entitiesName + type → role → why it exists

Phase 2 — Bottom-up rollup (RAPTOR-style). Each branch node summarises its children's summaries, deepest-first, producing a full multi-level summary tree.

Phase 3 — Document overview. Per-category root summaries are fused into one overview each, then into a single document-level "summary of summaries".

2.5Embedding

Runs two embedding passes per chunk — one for raw content and one for the LLM-generated summary — storing both as 384-dim vectors so a query can match either space.

PassText embedded
Content vectorRaw chunk content
Summary vector"section_name: summary" — name-prefixed so rare-term queries still match

Model: multi-qa-MiniLM-L6-cos-v1 (384-dim) — asymmetric Q→passage; useful cosine band ≈ 0.65–0.92 for relevant pairs. Ingestion and retrieval share this model so query and document vectors live in the same space. The aim provider calls a remote embeddings endpoint .

2.6Persistence (Milvus)

Upserts dual-vector chunks into Milvus in 200-row batches, auto-creating the collection with a full N-level tree schema on first use.

FieldTypePurpose
chunk_idVARCHAR(64) PKUnique chunk identifier
chunk_typeVARCHAR(32)One of the 6 extraction categories
sub_typeVARCHAR(32)Lifecycle action (install / configure / …)
depthINTTree depth (0 = root)
is_leafBOOLWhether this is a leaf node
parent_idVARCHAR(64)Parent chunk ID
children_idsVARCHAR(2048)JSON list of child IDs
contentVARCHAR(65535)Full chunk text
summaryVARCHAR(8192)LLM-generated summary
embeddingFLOAT_VECTOR(384)Content vector
summary_embeddingFLOAT_VECTOR(384)Summary vector

Supports both Milvus Lite (embedded single-file) and Milvus Standalone (remote Docker).

Lifecycle sub-types let retrieval scope by task: install · uninstall · upgrade · configure · integrate · administer · monitor · troubleshoot · use · reference · overview · other.

Part 03 · Read path

Retrieval Pipeline

Answers queries by searching Milvus with RRF fusion, re-ranking results, then either synthesising a grounded prose answer (informational) or an ordered execution plan (action).

Retrieval works over the whiteboard category set — Keywords, Personas, and Features, grounded and enriched with the Knowledge Base — while Workflows are fetched only on the action branch.

Endpoint: POST /api/v1/query/agentic — full agentic flow: rewrite → facets → intent → answer or plan.

3.1Basic retrieval

Embeds the query, runs an search on Milvus, and optionally expands each hit with its ancestor path and descendant subtree via a depth-first walk.

3.2Agentic retrieval

A multi-step pipeline that mirrors the knowledge-base flow: rewrite → facets → semantic fetch → intent branch → answer or plan → execute.

  1. Rewrite — expand acronyms, ground the query in the Knowledge Base context, produce up to 5 variants.
  2. Extract facets — the LLM pulls keywords, personas, and features from the query, grounded with the Knowledge Base.
  3. Fetch details — RRF search per facet (keywords / personas / features) across all query variants.
  4. Detect intent — heuristic: action verbs/phrases → action; "what is / define" → informational.
  5. Branch:
    • Action → sub-type scope → depth-first fetch of workflows → list top-k matching workflows + Knowledge + Keyword + Persona + Feature → extract ordered steps → synthesise a plan → execute & react.
    • Informational → collect Knowledge / keyword / persona / feature chunks → re-score & rank → synthesise an answer.

3.3RRF search

Fuses ranked results from multiple query variants and both vector fields using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 60).

For each query variant (original + up to 5 multi-queries):
    HNSW ANN on the summary vector  →  ranked list S
    HNSW ANN on the content vector  →  ranked list C   (run when top summary cosine < 0.85)

RRF score = Σ  1 / (60 + rank)   across all lists  →  deduplicated merged ranking

A content fallback (threshold 0.85) rescues chunks whose summary is poorly worded but whose raw content is a strong match.

3.4Answer & plan synthesis

Once RRF has produced a fused, deduplicated hit list, it is re-scored, then routed by intent into one of two synthesisers — grounded prose for informational queries, an ordered plan for action queries.

  • Re-score & rank — the fused hits are re-ordered by the scoring signals below.
  • Informational — the top chunks and their summaries are assembled into a context block and turned into grounded prose, together with the supporting chunks it drew from.
  • Action — the selected workflow's steps (walked in order), enriched with Knowledge + Keyword + Persona + Feature context, are turned into a numbered plan where each step carries an order, an action, a detail, and a source-chunk reference for traceability. If no steps are found, it falls back to answer synthesis.
